input: head is null or the first node of a finite, acyclic singly linked list of n distinct node objects, with 0 <= n <= 4294967295. Each caller-owned ListNode has ordinary writable data fields val and next; val is an integer in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], and next is another node or null. No getters, proxies, custom assignment behavior or concurrent observers/mutations are allowed. External aliases may point at any input node and observe the final rewiring. k is a positive integer in [1, 9007199254740991]. Integers are primitive safe-integer Numbers, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Containers are dense ordinary Arrays, excluding holes, proxies, subclasses and accessor-backed elements; strings are primitive, not boxed. Standard built-ins are unmodified and no concurrent mutation occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The original nodes arranged into reversed consecutive groups of exactly k nodes, with a final incomplete group left in its original order. The result is the new first original node or null; there are no copied output nodes. k = 1 preserves node order; an empty list returns null.
mutation_aliasing: Original node values and identities are preserved, but next fields in complete groups and connecting boundaries are rewired. The incomplete suffix has its own next edges unchanged. Caller aliases to nodes observe these changed links, including the original head becoming a group tail. No input node is lost, duplicated or replaced; the final list is acyclic and terminated by null. One private sentinel is allocated and not returned. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Node values are never arithmetically transformed. k and counters are exact safe integers; each k-node lookahead stops at the first absent node, so even a huge k cannot force iteration past the finite remaining list. The number of traversed nodes and loop counts fit the shared bound.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Every complete group is first checked and then reversed, and the final incomplete suffix is only checked. Reversal uses a saved following link and an after-group identity sentinel; no recursion or container of nodes is used.
